controls.title: The Story of Luca
paragraphs: Luca is a young sea monster. He lives under the water with his family. His parents tell him not to go to the surface. They say humans are dangerous. Luca is curious about the world above, but he must hide who he really is.

One day, Luca meets Alberto. Alberto is also a sea monster, but he lives on land. He shows Luca how to transform into a human. When sea monsters are dry, they look like humans. When they touch water, they change back into sea monsters. Luca is amazed.

Luca and Alberto go to a small Italian town called Portorosso. They want to buy a Vespa and explore the world together. But they must keep their identity a secret. In Portorosso, they meet a brave and friendly girl named Giulia.

Giulia invites them to join a local competition: a triathlon of swimming, eating pasta, and riding a bike. Luca and Alberto need to be careful. Swimming is part of the race, and water will reveal their secret. Luca starts to love being human. He wants to go to school and learn.

During the competition, it starts to rain. Luca and Alberto almost transform in front of everyone. Giulia helps them and keeps their secret. Luca learns that true friends trust each other and accept you for who you are.

In the end, Luca decides to follow his dream. He goes to school with Giulia. Alberto stays in Portorosso and finds a new family with Giulia's father. Their friendship changes, but it stays strong. Luca is happy being himself.

cards.title: Gerund (verb + -ing)
cards.body: We use the gerund after some verbs: enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, keep. We also use it after prepositions: good at, afraid of, tired of.
examples: Luca enjoys swimming in the sea.

cards.title: Infinitive (to + verb)
cards.body: We use the infinitive after verbs like want, decide, need, hope, plan, promise, offer. We also use it after adjectives: happy to, difficult to, important to.
examples: Luca wants to go to school.
They decided to join the competition.
It is difficult to hide your identity.

cards.title: Verbs that change meaning
cards.body: Some verbs can take both forms, but the meaning changes. Stop + gerund = finish an action. Stop + infinitive = stop in order to do something.
examples: Luca stopped to eat. (he stopped in order to eat)

cards.title: Gerund as subject
cards.body: We use a gerund (-ing form) as the subject of a sentence to talk about an activity or idea.

lessonFlow: Start with the Warm Up word association to activate vocabulary related to the sea, summer, and friendship. Ask the student to say the first word that comes to mind for each item.
Use the Lead-In opinion sort to discuss themes from the movie: friendship, secrets, adventure, and being different. This gets the student talking and introduces the topic.
Introduce target vocabulary through the definition match exercise. Then check understanding with the gap-fill sentences. If time allows, work through the phrasal verb practice.
Read the short story about Luca together aloud. Stop after each paragraph to check comprehension. Then let the student answer the quiz questions independently.
Present the grammar rules for infinitive vs. gerund using the rule cards. Explain each card clearly. Then let the student complete the rules and choose the correct options.
Move to controlled grammar practice. Start with the typing exercise (controlledInputPractice), then do the dropdown exercise. Check answers together.
Finish with the speaking questions. Encourage the student to give full answers using gerunds and infinitives. Use the Translation Time as extra practice or homework.
Add any useful links, vocabulary lists, or extra materials in the Resources section.
adaptationNotes: For stronger students: ask them to retell the Luca story in their own words after reading, using the target vocabulary.
For weaker students: pre-teach key vocabulary (sea monster, surface, transform, hide, secret) before the reading section. Read the text together and explain unknown words as you go.
If the student struggles with grammar: spend more time on the rule cards. Do the chooseCorrect exercise together and discuss why each answer is right.
For teens: focus more on the friendship and adventure themes. For adults: discuss the deeper themes of identity, life choices, and being true to yourself.
If time is short: skip the phrasal verb practice and the Translation Time. Assign Translation Time as homework.
